steps.show:
Larkspur Trading
3 minutesfrom gap to recovery

Fictional incident review · 14 October 2026
steps.say: This review follows a three-minute interruption at Larkspur Trading. We'll trace missing feed messages to a host setting, then explain how the next routine upgrade should be tested.

slides.title: Eighteen quiet minutes, then a burst

steps.show:
08:42:00
Driver upgrade completeprism-b01 passes quiet-feed checks
steps.say: At eight forty-two Vesper Standard Time, the B-channel host passed maintenance checks. Packets could arrive, but the checks did not test how much traffic the host could absorb at once.

steps.show:
09:00:00
Market opensPrism multicast traffic surges
steps.say: Eighteen minutes later, the open changed the workload abruptly. The opening burst demanded much more buffering than the quiet feed had needed, before packet processing could catch up.

steps.show:
09:00:00.240
B-channel sequence gap640 messages missing on prism-b01
steps.say: Within a quarter of a second, the handler detected missing sequence numbers. That locates the symptom at the open, but cannot tell us where the packets disappeared.

steps.show:
09:00:00.480
Risk haltKestrel instances stop on stale data
steps.say: Another quarter-second later, the freshness guard halted the strategy instances. This protective response stopped decisions on an incomplete market view while the feed problem was investigated.

steps.show:
09:03:00
Trading resumesMira validates prism-a01 and releases the halt
steps.say: About three minutes after the gap, Mira completed the move to the unchanged A channel. Fresh data restored trading, leaving the B-channel failure to be explained.

slides.title: Three possible places to lose packets

steps.show:
COULD NOT BE EXCLUDED

Exchange publication

Did Vesper Exchange omit messages from Prism?
steps.say: Initially, an exchange publication gap could not be excluded. Healthy receivers can report messages that were never sent, so we needed an independent account of publication.

steps.show:
COULD NOT BE EXCLUDED

Multicast membership

Did leaf-17 stop forwarding the subscribed group?
steps.say: A lost multicast membership could not be excluded either. That would interrupt delivery to the handler even if the exchange published every message.

steps.show:
COULD NOT BE EXCLUDED

Host receive path

Did prism-b01 run out of receive capacity?
steps.say: Host packet loss also could not be excluded. The recent driver change made it worth investigating, but timing alone was insufficient to confirm it as the cause.

steps.show: 640 missing messagesSymptom confirmed. Loss location still unknown.
steps.say: The highlighted line compares the next expected sequence with the next arrival. Their difference establishes missing messages. It confirms the symptom, while leaving all three possible loss locations open.

slides.title: Publication stayed continuous
slides.source: Vesper Exchange status page, Prism incident-window report

steps.show: Exchange gap ruled outThe report covers the incident window and both channels.
steps.say: The highlighted report explicitly checks publication continuity across the incident window. This is stronger than a green status badge. Within this fictional record, it rules out the exchange-gap hypothesis.

steps.show: Membership loss ruled outBoth feed subscriptions remained present throughout the window.
steps.say: The highlighted audit covers both handler ports throughout the failure window. No membership expired or left. That rules out membership loss, while leaving other switch faults outside this test.

slides.title: Receive misses rise at the open
slides.source: Host NIC counter snapshot and replay audit, prism-b01

steps.show: Host packet loss confirmed512 descriptors after upgrade; replay succeeds at 4096.
steps.say: The highlighted row's right-hand counter shows receive misses rising at the open. Replay reproduces loss with the smaller ring and clears it at the original capacity, confirming the host mechanism.

steps.show:
RULED OUT

Exchange publication gap

Incident-window publication report is continuous.
steps.say: The exchange-gap hypothesis is ruled out. The publication report covers the relevant interval, so missing messages at the receiver do not imply missing publication.

steps.show:
RULED OUT

Multicast membership loss

Switch audit shows uninterrupted subscriptions.
steps.say: The membership-loss hypothesis is ruled out. The switch retained the subscriptions. The conclusion stays narrow because this evidence addresses membership, rather than the whole network.

steps.show:
CONFIRMED

Host receive-ring exhaustion

Miss counters and controlled replay identify prism-b01.
steps.say: Host receive loss is confirmed. The counter timing locates the failure, and changing only ring capacity in replay explains why the new default failed under a burst.

slides.title: A default became a production limit

steps.show:
Previous receive ring4096
New driver default512

Descriptors available before packet processing catches up
steps.say: The driver reduced the receive ring to one eighth of its previous capacity. Because configuration inherited that default, a routine software change silently reduced the host's tolerance for short traffic bursts.

steps.show:
Opening burst exceeds buffer capacity

Receive misses cause a sequence gap, stale strategy data and a protective halt.
steps.say: The open supplied the trigger. The unpinned ring size supplied the vulnerability. A quiet health check could pass both configurations, which is why the missing burst test mattered.

steps.show:
01

Pin 4096 descriptors

Verify both hosts after reload and reboot.
steps.say: First, pin the ring size in configuration and verify it after reload and reboot. That makes the required capacity an explicit operating choice instead of an undocumented driver default.

steps.show:
02

Alert on receive misses

Trigger on a positive counter delta.
steps.say: Second, alert when receive misses increase. This gives Mira a direct signal from the failing layer, shortening the investigation instead of relying only on a downstream stale-data alarm.

steps.show:
03

Replay the pre-open burst

Require zero misses and zero gaps after every driver change.
steps.say: Finally, make a representative burst replay part of every driver change. Together, these checks preserve the capacity we depend on and prove it before the next market open.
